BandReason.description:
Why an item did not reach the top band.

An identifier, never copy: the sentence a reader sees is owned by the site
and can be rewritten without a schema change. A `high` item has no reason,
because there is nothing to explain.
BandReason.title: BandReason

ConfidenceBand.description: The band, not the number, is what drives behaviour and what a reader sees.
ConfidenceBand.title: ConfidenceBand

DigestViewItem.description:
One item, narrowed to what a page renders from it.

Every field here has a named renderer. The list is not "the published item
minus the big bits" - it is traced along the render path, and a field
without a reader does not earn the wire.

band_reason.description: Why the item is not in the top band. Null on a `high` item and on a day published before this existed - 14 of 3,733 committed items on 2026-08-31.

carried_by.description: How many feeds carried this one address. Null is unknown, never 1.
carried_by.title: Carried By

introduced_by_run.description: A global fact, true for every reader, asserted without any storage.
introduced_by_run.title: Introduced By Run

on_front_page.description: A salience feed voted for it. Null is unknown, never false.
on_front_page.title: On Front Page

rank_score.description: What the planning step scored the story at. Null is unknown, never 0.
rank_score.title: Rank Score

reader_note.description: Our sentence explaining a source limitation, never a badge.
reader_note.title: Reader Note

source_kind.description: Who is speaking. A vendor's own copy must not look like a reporter's.

time_source.description: Which clock `published_at` came from. Null reads as unknown: a page that prints a time without naming its clock cannot say which of the two it has.

truncated.description: The reader is told before they find out by clicking through.
truncated.title: Truncated

watchlist_hit.description: The story names a watchlist entity. Null is unknown, never false.
watchlist_hit.title: Watchlist Hit

DigestViewItem.title: DigestViewItem

DigestViewVisual.description: The rendered chart, as the `` needs it. `kind` is not here. It is read at build time off the committed tree for the console's chart count, and a browser drawing the image has no use for it.
DigestViewVisual.title: DigestViewVisual

LensId.description: A question asked of items already collected. Costs no extra request.
LensId.title: LensId

SourceKind.description:
What kind of speaker this is - the thing a reader uses to decide belief.

"A company said its product is faster" and "a reporter measured it" are not
the same claim, and without this they arrive looking identical. The
dangerous case is `announcement`: forwarding a vendor's own copy without
knowing it was the vendor is how a reader ends up carrying an ad.
SourceKind.title: SourceKind

TimeSource.description:
Which clock the time on an item came from.

`rank.appeared_at` prefers the feed's own date and falls back to when we
first saw the address. Both answers used to land in one field, so nothing
downstream could tell them apart - and the fallback is the one a reader
would want flagged, because it is our clock and not the publisher's.
TimeSource.title: TimeSource

VisualState.description:
What became of the visual. "Could not make it" and "made it then threw it
away" are different facts, so they never share a member.
VisualState.title: VisualState

changelog.change: Initial shape: the day's items narrowed to what a page renders, carrying a version of their own.
changelog.why: The staged day payload was a thirteen-name array in a build script, which was enough while the only reader was our own archive page. A reading route is about to fetch this file, so a browser we cannot upgrade will parse it and its address stops being movable - which is a persisted shape and therefore a contract before logic reads it (Rule #3). The version is here from the first byte so that an older shell reading a newer payload has something to branch on. Nine names join the thirteen in the same commit, each with a named renderer: carried_by, watchlist_hit, on_front_page and rank_score for the lead block, published_at and time_source for the time rail, introduced_by_run for the run divider, lenses for the topic chips, and key_points for the in-page filter that reads them today. Measured 2026-08-31 over 11 committed days and 3,733 items, gzip -9: 361.10 bytes an item before and 468.58 after, against 792.65 for the committed day.
